prompt: Was the founder of the bank that was established 42 years before the National Banking Act was expanded to include the Territory of Hawai'i still alive when it acquired Pioneer Federal Savings Bank?
answer: No. The bank was First Hawaiian Bank, founded in 1858 as Bishop & Co. by Charles Reed Bishop and William A. Aldrich—42 years before U.S. national banking laws were extended to the Territory of Hawaiʻi in 1900. Bishop died in 1915, while First Hawaiian acquired Pioneer Federal Savings Bank on August 6, 1993. Therefore, its founder was not alive at the time of the acquisition.
